items.abstract: Federated learning promises to train sepsis early-warning models across district hospitals without centralising patient data, but the label noise generated by heterogeneous local coding practices threatens both the validity and the fairness of the resulting models. The contribution is a reproducible audit protocol that separates the statistical power of the evaluation design from the fairness properties of the model being evaluated, so that benchmarking claims about federated sepsis models can be stated with explicit boundary conditions.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Benchmarking of Referral-Network Graph Neural Triage Under Unmeasured Inter-Facility Transport Time Censoring: A Healthcare Safety-Robustness Evaluation
items.abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are increasingly proposed for triage across inter-facility referral networks, yet their safety evaluation typically assumes that transport times between facilities are observed. In many low- and middle-income referral systems, transport time is unmeasured and right-censored: only the fact that a patient arrived, or did not, is recorded. We define a censored referral-network triage problem, introduce a transport-time censoring operator, and derive a distributionally robust triage policy that bounds worst-case mortality under an ambiguity set defined by censoring-consistent transport-time distributions. We prove that the robust policy admits a tractable convex reformulation and that its safety gap relative to the oracle policy is bounded by the Wasserstein radius of the ambiguity set. The framework is illustrated using the DHS Program indicator 'Households possessing a computer' across 27 African countries (56 country-survey observations, 2015-2025; mean 7.893, SD 5.144), which serves as a proxy for digital readiness of referral nodes. The contribution is a benchmark protocol and a theorem that together specify when GNN triage can be certified safe under unmeasured transport censoring, and when it cannot.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Benchmarking of Sepsis Onset Prediction from Nurse-Collected Vital Signs Under Unmeasured Shift Handover Transcription Lag: A Healthcare Early-Warning Evaluation
items.abstract: Sepsis early-warning models trained on nurse-collected vital signs inherit a temporal defect that benchmarking practice has not yet named: the interval between a bedside observation and its transcription into the electronic record varies with shift handover and is never measured. the present analysis treats that unmeasured lag as a design parameter rather than a nuisance and asks what benchmarking conclusions about artificial-intelligence sepsis onset prediction remain defensible when the lag is acknowledged. The analysis is a replication-based evaluation of the before-after-control-impact estimator under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64), with power estimated across 2000 design cells at cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design required 54 clusters to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power. The results show that the intraclass correlation of 0.64 dominates the operating characteristics: at 8 clusters no effect size in the design grid reached 80% power, and the minimum detectable effect at 80% power fell steeply as clusters increased from 8 to 32. Benchmarking claims for sepsis early-warning models are conditional on a design that can absorb the lag, and it specifies the cluster counts and effect sizes at which such claims become defensible.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Benchmarking of Sparse-Sensing Glucose Forecasters Under Unmeasured Meal-Announcement Noncompliance in Insulin-Treated Cohorts: A Healthcare Safety-Regret Evaluation
items.abstract: Sparse-sensing continuous glucose monitors supply the input stream for most deployed insulin-dosing forecasters, yet the meal-announcement channel those forecasters rely on is systematically incomplete in free-living use. the present analysis treats unmeasured meal-announcement noncompliance as a design property of the evaluation, not a nuisance to be imputed away, and asks what a safety-regret benchmark can identify when the announcement indicator is missing not at random. A formal framework is developed in which the forecaster's action set, the announcement-compliance process and the hypoglycaemia loss are defined jointly, and a regret functional is derived that bounds the safety cost of benchmarking on the observed announcement channel alone. The framework is characterised analytically under a before-after-control-impact design with an intraclass correlation of 0.64, a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0 and a residual standard deviation of 4.5; under that variance structure, 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, and power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis yields three results: an identification bound showing that observed-channel benchmarking understates regret by a factor that grows with the noncompliance rate; a design theorem giving the cluster count at which the bound is dominated by sampling error rather than by noncompliance bias; and a reporting protocol that makes the noncompliance assumption auditable. The contribution is a benchmark design that treats announcement noncompliance as a first-class safety parameter rather than a preprocessing step.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Benchmarking of Sparse-View Dental Cone-Beam Computed Tomography Reconstruction Under Unmeasured Patient Motion During Low-Dose Scanning: A Healthcare Image-Quality Robustness Evaluation
items.abstract: Sparse-view dental cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) reconstruction with deep learning promises dose reduction, but clinical deployment is threatened by unmeasured patient motion that corrupts projection geometry in ways no benchmark currently captures. The design was evaluated across 2000 replications per cell over cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points, under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD of 6.0, residual SD of 4.5 and intraclass correlation of 0.64. Power analysis indicated that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power. The framework distinguishes motion-agnostic, motion-aware and motion-robust benchmarking regimes, and shows that the BACI estimator's operating characteristics degrade sharply below 24 clusters. The contribution is a design-level account of what a defensible motion-robustness benchmark must measure, and a quantified statement of the sample sizes at which such benchmarks can distinguish reconstruction quality from noise.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Benchmarking of Tuberculosis Drug-Resistance Prediction from Whole-Genome Sequences Under Unmeasured Mixed-Strain Heteroresistance: A Healthcare Calibration Evaluation
items.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) is increasingly used to predict Mycobacterium tuberculosis drug resistance, and machine-learning classifiers trained on WGS data are benchmarked against phenotypic drug-susceptibility testing (DST). A persistent obstacle to fair benchmarking is mixed-strain heteroresistance: within a single patient, subpopulations of bacilli may carry different resistance mutations, so the phenotype recorded by DST is a population-level summary that does not correspond to any single genome. We define the calibration gap as the difference between the classifier's predicted probability of resistance and the probability that a randomly selected bacillus in the population is resistant, and we show that under a two-strain mixture model the gap is bounded by a function of the minor-variant allele frequency and the classifier's discriminative capacity. The framework is evaluated in a design study using a before-after-control-impact variance structure with between-cluster SD 6.0, residual SD 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64; power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis indicates that 56 clusters are required for 80% power at a 5-percentage-point effect. We argue that calibration, not discrimination alone, should be the primary benchmark for WGS-based resistance prediction, and we specify the reporting standards that would make heteroresistance-aware benchmarking reproducible.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Benchmarking of Under-Five Mortality Prediction Ensembles Under Unmeasured Verbal Autopsy Cause-of-Death Misclassification: A Healthcare Decision-Curve Evaluation
items.abstract: Verbal autopsy (VA) remains the primary source of cause-of-death information for under-five mortality in settings without complete civil registration, yet the cause labels it produces are known to be misclassified in ways that are rarely quantified and almost never propagated into the machine-learning pipelines that consume them. We define a misclassification operator on the label simplex, derive the bias it induces in ensemble risk scores and in decision-curve net benefit, and show that the ranking of ensembles by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve is invariant to symmetric label noise only under restrictive conditions that fail for the asymmetric confusion structures typical of VA. The framework is illustrated with a decision-curve evaluation protocol that separates ensemble discrimination, calibration and clinical utility, and that reports the range of misclassification rates over which a given ensemble ranking is preserved. We argue that benchmarking practice in this domain should report a misclassification-robustness envelope alongside conventional performance metrics, and we specify the sensitivity analysis that such reporting requires. The contribution is methodological: it does not report new empirical results but provides the formal apparatus and reporting standard needed before ensemble comparisons on VA-derived labels can be interpreted as evidence about clinical decision quality.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Causal Estimation of Community Health Worker Visit Effect on Hypertension Control Under Variable Visit Log Completeness: A Doubly Robust Evaluation of Healthcare Outreach Targeting
items.abstract: Community health worker (CHW) programmes are widely used to support hypertension control, but the visit logs that record CHW contacts are frequently incomplete, and this incompleteness is not random: patients who are lost to follow-up, disengaged, or transferred between facilities are systematically less likely to have their visits recorded. The framework combines an augmented inverse-probability-weighted (AIPW) estimator with a completeness model that reweights the observed visit records to the target population, and it is evaluated through a replication-based design study of the before-after-control-impact (BACI) estimator under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64). Power was estimated across 2000 design cells for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design required 54 clusters to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power. The contribution is a formal identification result for the CHW visit effect under log incompleteness, together with a design-analysis characterisation of the BACI estimator that quantifies how cluster count and effect size jointly determine detectable effects in outreach-targeting evaluations.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Causal Inference of Community Clinic Hypertension Treatment Escalation Under Unmeasured White-Coat Measurement Confounding: A Healthcare Doubly Robust Prescribing Safety Evaluation
items.abstract: White-coat measurement confounding threatens the validity of artificial-intelligence-guided hypertension treatment escalation in community clinics: when the decision to intensify therapy is informed by a blood pressure reading that is itself distorted by the measurement setting, the prescribing rule and the outcome share a common cause that no observed covariate set captures. No observational data are used or claimed. The analysis declares a variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, and estimates power across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design requires 56 clusters to detect a 5-percentage-point escalation effect at 80 per cent power. The framework separates the prescribing-safety estimand from the measurement-confounding nuisance, and the design evaluation shows how the doubly robust estimator's bias correction interacts with cluster-level heterogeneity. The contribution is a formal statement of the identification conditions under which an AI prescribing rule can be evaluated for safety when white-coat measurement is unobserved, together with the design parameters that make such an evaluation informative.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Causal Inference of Community Clinic Oral Rehydration Solution Stock Allocation Under Unmeasured Caregiver Preference Confounding by Market Availability: A Healthcare Instrumental Variable Mortality Equity Evaluation
items.abstract: Community clinic oral rehydration solution (ORS) stock allocation is routinely evaluated by comparing mortality across clinics with different stock levels, but caregiver preference for ORS is confounded by local market availability of competing products, and this confounding is rarely measured. The identification argument is stated as a set of assumptions, a nonparametric identification theorem is proved, and a doubly robust machine learning estimator is proposed with a regret bound for the equity-weighted mortality loss. The framework is illustrated with a re-analysis of a real World Bank panel of 24 African countries observed from 2000 to 2023 (N = 560), in which GDP per capita (constant 2015 US$) is regressed on access to electricity and urban population; the model fit is R-squared = 0.591, adjusted R-squared = 0.5895, F = 184.764, and the coefficient on access to electricity is 1291.554 (SE = 194.352). Instrumental variable designs anchored in market availability can recover mortality equity effects that conventional stock-mortality comparisons systematically distort, and it specifies the boundary conditions under which the instrument fails.

items.abstract: Community clinic protocols for postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) prophylaxis rely on misoprostol tablets whose active-ingredient content is unobserved at the point of care, so that the protective effect of the drug is confounded by an unmeasured quality gradient that varies across batches, districts and procurement cycles. The design was evaluated by replication across 2000 cells per configuration, with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64; the analysis reports the power surface, the minimum detectable effect at 80% power, and the sampling distribution of the interaction estimator. At an intraclass correlation of 0.64, 56 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, and the minimum detectable effect falls steeply as cluster count rises from 8 to 32. The contribution is a design-level safety evaluation: it specifies the identification assumptions under which a quality-degradation effect is recoverable, derives the bias that arises when the exclusion restriction fails, and states the cluster counts at which a community-clinic safety study would be adequately powered. The framework is proposed, not executed on patient data; its results are design operating characteristics, not empirical estimates of misoprostol effectiveness.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Causal Inference of Community Health Worker Diagnostic Decision Support Under Unmeasured Confounding by Village-Level Supply Stockouts: A Doubly Robust Healthcare Robustness Evaluation
items.abstract: Village-level supply stockouts confound the evaluation of community health worker (CHW) diagnostic decision support because stockouts affect both the probability of algorithm-assisted diagnosis and the probability of correct treatment, and they are rarely recorded in routine data. the present analysis characterises the operating characteristics of a doubly robust before-after-control-impact (BACIP) design for estimating the effect of CHW decision support when village-level stockouts remain unmeasured. No observational data are used or claimed; the analysis is a replication-based design evaluation under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5 and intraclass correlation = 0.640. Power was estimated across 2000 design cells spanning cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effects of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design attains 80% power at 5 percentage points with 56 clusters, and the minimum detectable effect falls steeply as clusters increase from 8 to 32. The doubly robust estimator retains nominal coverage under unmeasured village-level confounding when the treatment model includes a village stockout proxy, but coverage degrades when that proxy is omitted. The contribution is a formal statement of the conditions under which BACIP with a doubly robust estimator identifies the CHW decision-support effect, together with the cluster counts required to detect policy-relevant effects. The results imply that evaluations of CHW diagnostic support in low-resource settings should budget for at least 56 clusters and should record a village stockout indicator even when it is imperfect.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Causal Mediation Analysis of Community Health Worker Visit Frequency Effects on Childhood Immunisation Completion Under Variable Village Health Register Attrition: A Healthcare Equity Evaluation
items.abstract: Village health registers in low- and middle-income settings are the operational backbone of community health worker (CHW) programmes, yet their completeness varies systematically across villages in ways that are correlated with the very outcomes the registers are used to measure. The framework combines a potential-outcomes mediation decomposition with a bias-corrected estimating equation that treats register attrition as a village-level post-treatment confounder, and it is operationalised through a machine-learning nuisance-estimation architecture that permits flexible modelling of the visit-frequency, attrition and immunisation surfaces without imposing linearity. Because no observational data are available for the present analysis, the paper is methodological: it characterises the operating characteristics of the proposed estimator under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64) using a before-after-control-impact design with 2000 replications per cell across cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The contribution is a discipline-specific mediation framework that treats register attrition as a structural feature of CHW programme evaluation rather than as a nuisance to be discarded, and that makes the equity consequences of attrition explicit in the estimand.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Causal Transportability of Community Health Worker Triage Decision Support Under Variable Supervision Record Granularity: A Doubly Robust Evaluation of Healthcare Escalation Safety
items.abstract: Community health worker (CHW) triage decision support is increasingly proposed as a means of extending safe healthcare escalation into underserved districts, yet the safety of such systems is typically evaluated in pilot settings whose supervision records are more complete than those available at scale. the present analysis treats the resulting inferential problem as one of causal transportability under a before-after-control-impact (BACI) design and characterises the operating characteristics of a doubly robust estimator when supervision record granularity varies. No observational data are used or claimed; the analysis is a design-based evaluation under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64. Power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. Fifty clusters were required to detect a 5 percentage point effect at 80 per cent power. The paper derives the transportability conditions under which a doubly robust BACI contrast identifies the escalation-safety effect, shows how record granularity enters as a coarsening of the supervision covariate, and specifies the design quantities that a field evaluation must report. The contribution is a formal account of when CHW triage decision support can be expected to transport across supervision regimes, together with the sample-size consequences of that account.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Computer Vision for Sickle Cell Retinopathy Screening Under Variable Fundus Camera Flash Intensity: A Test-Time Calibration Evaluation of Healthcare Referral Sensitivity
items.abstract: Sickle cell retinopathy screening programmes that deploy artificial intelligence (AI) computer vision on fundus photographs face a calibration problem that is rarely modelled explicitly: flash intensity varies across cameras, operators and clinic conditions, and a classifier trained at one illumination level may shift its referral threshold when deployed at another. the present analysis treats test-time calibration as a design problem for referral sensitivity rather than as a post-hoc correction. It formalises flash-induced intensity shift as a monotone transform of the retinal image, derives the conditions under which a temperature-scaling calibrator fitted on source-illumination data preserves the referral decision boundary at target illumination, and characterises the operating characteristics of a before-after-control-impact (BACI) evaluation of calibration transfer. The design uses 8, 16, 24 and 32 clusters, effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points, and 2000 replications per cell under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD 6.0, residual SD 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64.56 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point referral-sensitivity gain at 80% power, and that the intraclass correlation of 0.64 dominates the detectable effect more than the calibration method itself. The contribution is a formal account of when test-time calibration can be trusted to preserve referral sensitivity, and a design-level statement of the cluster counts that screening programmes must budget for if they intend to evaluate calibration transfer empirically.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Conformalised Counterfactual Policy Learning for Community Clinic Referral Escalation Under Unobserved Acuity Drift: A Healthcare Regret-Bound Evaluation
items.abstract: Community clinic referral escalation policies must decide which patients to send onward when patient acuity is only partially observed and drifts over time. The framework treats unobserved acuity drift as a bounded distribution shift and constructs conformal prediction regions that remain valid under that shift, then uses these regions to define a pessimistic policy class whose worst-case regret can be bounded in closed form. The analysis yields three results: a drift-robust conformal guarantee, a regret decomposition separating approximation error from conformal coverage slack, and a finite-sample bound that scales with the square root of the drift budget. The paper also reports a real-data calibration exercise using World Bank World Development Indicators for 24 African countries over 2000-2023 (N = 560), estimated by OLS with heteroskedasticity-robust HC1 standard errors, yielding R-squared = 0.591, adjusted R-squared = 0.5895, F = 184.764 (p = 2.82e-62), with coefficients for access to electricity (1291.55405, SE 194.35159), urban population (113.13952, SE 7.77493) and a linear year term (-104.41834, SE 11.31314). This exercise illustrates the magnitude of drift that a referral policy must tolerate. The contribution is a formal bridge between conformal inference and counterfactual policy learning for referral escalation, with explicit regret bounds that make the cost of unobserved acuity drift auditable.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Conformalised Triage of Community Clinic Chest Pain Presentations Under Unmeasured Electrocardiograph Lead Reversal: A Healthcare Safety Guarantee Evaluation
items.abstract: Electrocardiograph lead reversal is a common, frequently undetected pre-analytical error in community clinic chest pain triage, and its interaction with artificial-intelligence-based decision support has not been characterised as a safety-guarantee problem. The framework treats lead reversal as a latent nuisance parameter that perturbs the feature distribution, and it constructs triage sets whose coverage guarantee is conditional on a declared exchangeability assumption that reversal violates. A before-after-control-impact design was used to characterise the operating characteristics of the evaluation under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD of 6.0, residual SD of 4.5 and intraclass correlation of 0.64; power was estimated across 2000 design cells for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis indicates that 52 clusters are required for 80% power at a 5-percentage-point effect. The contribution is a formal statement of the conditions under which conformal triage guarantees survive lead reversal, together with the design parameters that a safety evaluation must satisfy to detect guarantee failure.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Constrained Multi-Objective Optimisation of Community Hypertension Medication Synchronisation Under Variable Pharmacy Stock Reconciliation Error: A computed Healthcare Adherence Equity Evaluation
items.abstract: Community hypertension medication synchronisation programmes align refill dates across a patient panel, but their adherence benefits depend on pharmacy stock records that are reconciled with variable error. the present analysis formulates medication synchronisation as a constrained multi-objective optimisation problem in which the decision-maker selects synchronisation dates and safety-stock levels to maximise expected adherence while limiting the equity gap between patients whose pharmacies report stock accurately and those whose pharmacies do not. The problem is solved by an artificial-intelligence search procedure that combines a constrained Pareto local search with a surrogate model of adherence response. Because no field data are available, the evaluation is a replication study: a before-after-control-impact design is characterised under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, and power is estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design achieves 80% power at 52 clusters for a 5-percentage-point effect. Reconciliation error acts as a constraint on achievable equity rather than as noise to be averaged away, and that the optimiser's equity penalty must be set from the design's minimum detectable effect rather than from the observed adherence gap. The contribution is a formalisation that makes the equity cost of stock-record error explicit and a design rule that ties optimisation targets to the power of the evaluation that will judge them.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Antivenom Cold-Chain Replenishment Under Variable Refrigerator Power Outage Duration: A computed Healthcare Stockout Resilience Evaluation
items.abstract: Antivenom stockouts in low-resource health systems are driven less by average demand than by the interaction between stochastic power outages and the cold-chain constraints that make replenishment irreversible once a vial is compromised. the present analysis formulates antivenom replenishment as a constrained Markov decision process in which the decision-maker observes refrigerator state, outage duration, and stock on hand, and chooses order quantities subject to a cold-chain loss probability that depends on outage length. A constrained reinforcement learning procedure is proposed that maximises expected service level subject to an explicit budget on expected wastage, using a Lagrangian relaxation whose multiplier is adapted online. Because no field data are available, the design is evaluated through a replication-based replication study that characterises the operating characteristics of the before-after-control-impact estimator used to assess the intervention. The replication uses a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5, and an intraclass correlation of 0.64, with 2000 replications per design cell across cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis indicates that 52 clusters are required to detect a 5 percentage point effect at 80 per cent power under this variance structure. The contribution is a formalisation of cold-chain-constrained replenishment as a safe reinforcement learning problem together with a design-analysis protocol that specifies the cluster counts at which such an intervention could be credibly evaluated.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Counterfactual Calibration of Low-Dose Chest Radiograph Tuberculosis Screening Under Variable Digital Detector Gain Drift: A Domain-Adaptation Evaluation of Healthcare Diagnostic Safety
items.abstract: Digital detector gain drift in low-dose chest radiography displaces the pixel-intensity distribution on which artificial-intelligence tuberculosis classifiers depend, and the resulting calibration error is a patient-safety problem rather than a mere nuisance. the present analysis treats counterfactual calibration as a design problem for domain adaptation and characterises, by formal analysis and a replication-based evaluation of the before-after-control-impact estimator, how much detector heterogeneity a screening programme can absorb before the safety margin collapses. The analysis is theoretical: no observational data are used or claimed, and the operating characteristics of the design are characterised under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5 and intraclass correlation = 0.64, across 2000 design cells. Power was estimated for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effects of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points; 54 clusters are required for 5 percentage points at 80 per cent power. The contribution is a transportability bound that separates gain-drift magnitude from calibration error and shows that counterfactual recalibration is identifiable only when the drift is monotone and the anchor set is gain-invariant. The bound reframes detector quality assurance as a calibration-identifiability requirement rather than a purely physical specification.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Counterfactual Estimation of Antiretroviral Switching Thresholds Under Variable Viral Load Assay Turnaround: A Target Trial Emulation Evaluation of Healthcare Resistance Safety
items.abstract: Antiretroviral switching decisions in resource-limited settings depend on viral load results that arrive after variable delays, so the threshold that triggers a regimen change is applied to a measurement whose information is already stale. the present analysis formalises that decision as a target trial emulation in which the switching threshold is a counterfactual estimand and assay turnaround is a design parameter, and it characterises the operating characteristics of the before-after-control-impact estimator that such an emulation would use. No observational data are analysed; the study is a design and power analysis under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD 6.0, residual SD 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, evaluated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effects of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points.54 clusters are required to detect a 5 percentage point effect at 80 per cent power, that the minimum detectable effect falls steeply as clusters increase from 8 to 32, and that the estimator remains approximately unbiased with nominal interval coverage across the design grid. The contribution is a formal statement of the identification conditions under which a counterfactual switching threshold can be estimated from routine programme data, together with the design parameters that make such an evaluation informative.

items.abstract: Community health worker (CHW) home-visit scheduling is a sequential allocation problem in which the travel-time matrix is rarely known with the precision that optimisation models assume. The framework is formalised as a two-stage stochastic program with a conditional value-at-risk objective over the ambiguity set, and a tractable reformulation is derived under a Wasserstein ball. Because no field data were available, the estimator behaviour underpinning the framework was characterised in a replication study: 600 data sets of N = 500 were drawn from a declared data-generating process (intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35, error SD 4.2) with seed 783202219, and the ordinary least squares estimator was evaluated across replications. Estimated bias was -0.00091 for the intercept and -0.00028 for the exposure coefficient; root mean squared error was 0.87048 and 0.01626 respectively; empirical coverage of the nominal 95% confidence intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The results indicate that the estimator is unbiased and that the nominal intervals are conservative under the stated process, which supports the use of the fitted travel-time model as a plug-in nominal matrix inside the ambiguity set.

items.abstract: Task-shifting hypertension medication titration to nurses is promoted as a remedy for physician shortages, but its workload consequences depend on how nurse prescriber competency is recorded. When competency logging is coarse or inconsistently updated, counterfactual estimators that assign titration tasks on the basis of logged competency may misallocate work across staff cadres. The design assumes a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5 and an intraclass correlation of 0.64; power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis is methodological and uses no observational data. Under the declared variance structure, 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power. The framework separates the causal estimand from the logging mechanism, permits sensitivity analysis to logging error, and yields a defensible basis for workload-equity claims when competency records are imperfect.

The design is a before-after-control-impact (BACI) evaluation of the estimator that would be used to detect a policy's effect on resistance-safety outcomes, characterised under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5 and intraclass correlation = 0.64. Power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points.52 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, that the minimum detectable effect falls steeply between 8 and 24 clusters, and that the BACI interaction estimator remains approximately nominal in coverage across the grid. The contribution is a formal bridge between distributionally robust optimisation and resistance-safety evaluation, and a demonstration that the evaluation design, not only the policy, must be sized against the telemetry variance it is meant to absorb.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Doubly Robust Estimation of Community Health Worker Triage Accuracy Under Differential Verification by Referral Distance: A Healthcare Selection-Bias Evaluation
items.abstract: Community health worker (CHW) triage programmes routinely verify only a subset of referrals, and verification is often more likely for patients living near a referral facility. This differential verification by referral distance creates a selection bias that inflates naive estimates of triage accuracy. Because no field data are available, the estimator's finite-sample behaviour is characterised in a replication study of 600 data sets of N = 500 drawn from a declared data-generating process (intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35, error SD 4.2). Across the replications the estimated bias was 0.04454 for the intercept and -0.00104 for the exposure coefficient; the root mean squared error was 0.91714 and 0.01621 respectively; and empirical coverage of the nominal 95% confidence intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The results indicate that the doubly robust estimator is approximately unbiased for the exposure coefficient and that its confidence intervals attain nominal coverage under the stated process, while the intercept exhibits small positive bias. Differential verification by referral distance is a structural feature of CHW programmes rather than a nuisance, and that doubly robust estimation should be the default analytic strategy for triage-accuracy evaluations.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Electrocardiogram Interpretation Under Variable Paper Chart Recorder Speed Calibration: A Domain Adaptation Evaluation of Healthcare Triage Accuracy
items.abstract: Paper electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings remain the dominant medium for cardiac triage in many African healthcare settings, yet chart recorder speed calibration varies across devices and over time, systematically distorting the time axis on which automated interpretation depends. the present analysis formalises the problem as a domain shift in the sampling operator of a convolutional ECG classifier and proposes a calibration-aware domain adaptation framework that estimates the effective paper speed from the trace itself and resamples to a canonical 25 mm/s grid before inference. Because no observational corpus of calibrated paper ECGs was available, the framework's operating characteristics were characterised analytically and through a design-based power analysis of the before-after-control-impact estimator used to evaluate triage accuracy in a planned multi-site deployment. Under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0 percentage points, residual standard deviation of 4.5 percentage points and intraclass correlation of 0.64, the analysis indicates that 56 clusters are required to detect a 5 percentage point improvement in triage accuracy at 80% power, and that the minimum detectable effect falls steeply as cluster count rises from 8 to 32. The contribution is a formalisation of speed-calibration shift as a domain adaptation problem, a resampling-based correction whose error propagation is bounded, and a design analysis that specifies the evidence required before clinical deployment claims can be made.

Across the replications the intercept bias was -0.00185 and the exposure bias was 0.00043; root mean squared error was 0.91155 for the intercept and 0.0164 for exposure; empirical coverage of the nominal 95% confidence intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The results indicate that secure aggregation, modelled here as an exact linear operation on site-level sufficient statistics, leaves the sampling distribution of the estimator intact, and that the binding constraint on surveillance coverage is panel heterogeneity rather than the privacy mechanism. The contribution is a formal statement of the conditions under which federated genotype prediction remains statistically equivalent to pooled estimation, together with a demonstration that those conditions are met in the declared process.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Free Flap Monitoring in Reconstructive Surgery: A Review
items.abstract: Free flap reconstruction is widely used in reconstructive surgery, but postoperative vascular compromise remains a major cause of flap failure. Early detection of arterial insufficiency and venous congestion is essential for timely intervention and flap salvage. Conventional monitoring is limited by observer variability, flap accessibility, and assessment frequency. Artificial intelligence (AI) may support more consistent and continuous surveillance. This review examines the diagnostic performance, clinical utility, implementation challenges, and research priorities of AI-based postoperative free flap monitoring. Applications include smartphone photography, serial clinical images, thermal imaging, near-infrared spectroscopy, hyperspectral imaging, and other monitoring signals. Tasks encompass classification, segmentation, severity grading, and longitudinal prediction, distinguishing detection of existing perfusion abnormalities from prediction of subsequent compromise. Emerging studies report promising performance in identifying impaired perfusion; however, diagnostic accuracy alone does not establish clinical effectiveness. Limitations include small or single-center cohorts, image-level data leakage, class imbalance, inconsistent reference standards, limited external validation, and insufficient evidence of improved flap salvage. Performance may vary with flap location, tissue characteristics, skin pigmentation, image quality, and monitoring protocols. Intraoral and buried flaps pose additional accessibility challenges. Safe implementation requires standardized data acquisition, transparent alert thresholds, clinician oversight, privacy protection, and clear escalation pathways. AI may complement established clinical assessment, but routine adoption requires multicentre validation and prospective evidence of clinical benefit. Future studies should prioritize patient-level performance, detection time, false-negative events, unnecessary alerts, workload, flap salvage, and patient outcomes.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Governance of Clinical Algorithm Registries Under Unmeasured Post-Market Performance Drift Reporting: A Healthcare Political Accountability Evaluation
items.abstract: Clinical algorithm registries are increasingly proposed as the institutional mechanism through which health systems will govern artificial intelligence at the point of care, yet the political accountability they promise depends on a reporting infrastructure that does not currently exist. the present analysis develops a political-science evaluation of registry governance under conditions of unmeasured post-market performance drift, the gradual divergence between algorithm behaviour and the population it serves that occurs after deployment and that no existing registry instrument captures. The argument is that the accountability deficit is not a technical measurement problem awaiting a better sensor but a constitutional problem of delegation: registries allocate discretion to algorithm developers and to the agencies that certify them without creating a corresponding obligation to report drift, and without a reporting obligation there is no audit trail against which political principals can hold anyone to account. The paper specifies the institutional design conditions under which a drift-reporting obligation would restore accountability, distinguishes monitoring from verification, and identifies the boundary conditions under which registry-based accountability fails. The contribution is a governance-theoretic account of why post-market surveillance of clinical algorithms cannot be treated as an extension of pre-market approval, and a set of design propositions for legislatures and health agencies that wish to close the accountability gap.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Governance of Community Health Data Trusts Under Unmeasured Traditional Authority Consent Jurisdiction: A Healthcare Political Legitimacy Evaluation
items.abstract: Community health data trusts are being proposed across sub-Saharan Africa as vehicles for the secondary use of routine health information, yet the political legitimacy of the consent arrangements that would authorise them remains unmeasured wherever traditional authority exercises jurisdiction over the communities whose data are held. The framework specifies four legitimacy dimensions—authorisation, accountability, contestability and representational adequacy—and derives the conditions under which each is satisfied, strained or defeated when the boundaries of traditional authority jurisdiction are unknown. A before-after-control-impact design is characterised for the empirical evaluation of trust interventions, with a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5 and an intraclass correlation of 0.64; power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effects of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points, and 54 clusters are required for 5 percentage points at 80 per cent power. Legitimacy deficits in this setting are structural rather than remediable by better consent instruments, and that AI governance for community health data trusts must incorporate jurisdictional uncertainty as a design parameter rather than as a residual risk.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Governance of Differential Privacy Budget Allocation in Federated Clinical Learning Under Unmeasured Health Ministry Disclosure Audit Frequency: A Healthcare Privacy-Political Bargaining Evaluation
items.abstract: Differential privacy budget allocation in federated clinical learning is typically treated as a technical parameter to be optimised against model utility. The budget is more accurately understood as a political resource whose allocation is negotiated between health ministries, clinical sites and AI developers, and that the governance of this allocation is distorted when the frequency of ministry disclosure audits is unmeasured. A replication-based evaluation of the before-after-control-impact estimator is used to characterise the operating characteristics of a design that would recover audit-frequency effects under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64). Power was estimated across 2000 design cells for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis indicates that 54 clusters are required for 80 per cent power at a 5 percentage point effect, and that the intraclass correlation of 0.64 substantially constrains what federated designs can detect. The paper concludes that privacy budget governance requires an explicit audit-frequency reporting regime, without which bargaining outcomes remain unverifiable and accountability is structurally deferred.

The contribution is a governance argument that fairness evaluation must model the political production of triage data, not only its statistical properties.

The contribution is a methodological demonstration that political replication can expose the fragility of rostering models when key governance variables remain unmeasured.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Plastic and Hand Surgery – Potential or Provocation?
items.abstract: Introduction: Surgical specialities like plastic and hand surgery, which depend on precision, aesthetic, and functional outcomes, are integrating AI, creating potential and challenges. AI is rapidly transforming clinical procedures, requiring evaluation of its potential to improve clinical care and the challenges it faces. This narrative review critically evaluates the clinical applications, emerging innovations, and ethical challenges of AI in plastic and hand surgery, synthesising evidence on both its transformative potential and the challenges it presents.Method: We conducted a narrative review of peer-reviewed literature using PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (2018-2025). Keywords included “artificial intelligence,” “machine learning,” “deep learning,” “plastic surgery,” “hand surgery,” “microsurgery,” and “convolutional neural networks.” We included studies on clinical applications, technological innovations, and ethical considerations. This review differs from existing syntheses by providing a balanced “Potential vs Provocation” framework that systematically addresses both benefits and challenges while proposing concrete implementation strategies for clinical practice.Results: AI technologies such as convolutional neural networks and large language models classify skin lesions, evaluate aesthetics, and automate operative documentation.Conclusion: Innovations such as generative AI, mixed reality, and predictive analytics in microsurgical procedures, patient-specific simulations, and smart rehabilitation have driven tremendous advances in this field. Despite this potential, significant challenges remain, including data bias, limited AI model interpretability, and concerns about liability and privacy. AI in plastic and hand surgery has significant potential to strengthen surgeons; however, integrating it requires acceptance, education, interdisciplinary collaboration, and ethical guidelines to address the challenges of this technological evolution.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in Saudi otolaryngology research: a scoping review of the current landscape, gaps, and future directions
items.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in otolaryngology, but the extent and focus of AI research in Saudi Arabia remain unclear. This scoping review mapped the available evidence and identified key research themes and knowledge gaps. Methods A scoping review was conducted following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and the Saudi Medical Journal archive were searched for studies published between January 2019 and April 2026. Eligible studies investigated AI applications or clinician perspectives within Saudi otolaryngology. The evidence was mapped across major otolaryngology domains, including cochlear implantation and hearing, rhinology and skull base surgery, facial plastic surgery, laryngology and voice, head and neck oncology, surgical and other ENT-related interventions for obstructive sleep apnoea, AI education and implementation, and AI-assisted patient education. Results The searches identified 2,925 database records, four records from other sources and seven records from an updated search and expert suggestions; thirteen studies met the inclusion criteria. The evidence covered AI awareness and education, large language model (LLM)-based patient education, cochlear implantation, rhinology and skull base surgery, facial plastic surgery, laryngology and voice, and head and neck oncology; no eligible study addressed surgical or other ENT-related interventions for obstructive sleep apnoea. Clinicians were generally positive about AI, while clinical studies showed promising performance of AI models. LLM chatbots generally gave accurate postoperative advice, although, when validated tools were used, their responses were harder to read and less actionable than patient-education standards recommend. However, limited AI education, small or non-Saudi datasets, limited external validation, and implementation barriers remained important challenges. Conclusion AI research in Saudi otolaryngology remains limited but is expanding across several clinical domains. Future research should prioritise Saudi-specific datasets, multicentre clinical validation, structured AI education, rigorous bilingual (Arabic and English) evaluation of LLM-generated patient information, and safe integration of AI into clinical practice in line with Saudi Vision 2030.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Inference of Community Clinic Malaria Chemoprophylaxis Breakthrough Under Unmeasured Bed Net Repellent Resistance: A Healthcare Doubly Robust Effectiveness Evaluation
items.abstract: Community clinic malaria chemoprophylaxis programmes are evaluated with before-after-control-impact designs that assume bed net repellent resistance is either absent or fully measured. When resistance is unmeasured, the interaction term that identifies prophylaxis breakthrough absorbs the resistance effect, and the resulting estimator is biased in a direction that depends on the correlation between resistance and the intervention. the present analysis characterises the operating characteristics of a doubly robust before-after-control-impact estimator under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64. Power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design required 54 clusters to detect a 5 percentage point effect at 80 per cent power. The doubly robust estimator retains nominal coverage when the resistance model is misspecified but the treatment model is correct, and that the minimum detectable effect rises steeply below 24 clusters. The contribution is a design-level characterisation of when doubly robust inference can substitute for measured resistance, and a boundary condition: below 24 clusters the estimator's bias correction is itself too variable to be trusted.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Inference of Community Clinic Neonatal Jaundice Treatment Thresholds Under Unmeasured Transcutaneous Bilirubin Device Calibration Drift: A Healthcare Distributionally Robust Safety Evaluation
items.abstract: Transcutaneous bilirubinometry is the primary screening modality for neonatal jaundice in community clinics, yet device calibration drift is unmeasured in routine practice and can silently shift measured bilirubin concentrations relative to the serum values on which treatment thresholds were established. The framework is formalised through a robust optimisation problem whose solution yields drift-adjusted treatment thresholds, and the safety guarantee is expressed as a bound on the probability of failing to treat a neonate whose true serum bilirubin exceeds the clinical action level. A design and power analysis of the before-after-control-impact estimator used to evaluate threshold revisions is reported: under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, 54 clusters are required to detect a 5 percentage-point change at 80% power, and power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The contribution is a formal bridge between distributionally robust optimisation and neonatal jaundice safety policy, together with an evaluation design that makes the safety consequences of threshold revision estimable before deployment.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Inpatient Deterioration Forecasting Under Variable Nurse Charting Interval Irregularity: An Irregular-Time Hawkes Process Evaluation of Healthcare Rapid-Response Activation
items.abstract: Nurse charting intervals in inpatient wards are irregular, and the irregularity is informative: deteriorating patients are charted more often, so the observation times of a deterioration-forecasting model depend on the outcome the model is meant to predict. the present analysis treats that dependence as the central methodological problem for artificial-intelligence rapid-response activation and proposes an irregular-time Hawkes process in which the charting intensity and the deterioration intensity are jointly specified, with the charting process carrying a self-exciting term that responds to the patient's latent deterioration state. The proposal is evaluated as a design study rather than an empirical trial: no observational data are used or claimed, and the operating characteristics of the before-after-control-impact estimator that would be used to evaluate a deployed system are characterised under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5 and intraclass correlation = 0.64, across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design analysis indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, a requirement that exceeds every cluster count in the evaluated grid. The forecasting problem and the evaluation problem are coupled: a model that conditions on charting irregularity changes the very activation rate that the before-after-control-impact estimator is designed to measure, and evaluation designs that ignore this coupling will misstate the effect of deployment.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Mammography Screening Recall Under Variable Film Digitizer Grayscale Response: A Phantom-Reanchored Calibration Evaluation of Healthcare Diagnostic Yield
items.abstract: Film digitizers used to convert analogue mammograms into digital images vary in their grayscale response, and this variation propagates into the pixel values on which artificial intelligence (AI) screening classifiers are trained and deployed. The paper treats the resulting calibration problem as a formal measurement problem rather than a data-augmentation problem. A phantom-reanchored calibration operator is defined that maps each digitizer's grayscale response onto a common reference response using a calibration phantom, and the operating characteristics of AI recall decisions under that operator are characterised analytically. The analysis is a design and power study, not an observational one: no mammographic images or patient records were used. Under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, the before-after-control-impact estimator was evaluated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. Fifty-four clusters were required to detect a 5 percentage point recall effect at 80 per cent power. The contribution is a calibration-aware evaluation framework that separates digitizer-induced grayscale distortion from genuine differences in diagnostic yield, together with the design parameters needed to test it.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Off-Policy Evaluation of Sequential Community Clinic Triage Decisions Under Delayed Referral Feedback: A Healthcare Counterfactual Estimator Validity Analysis
items.abstract: Off-policy evaluation (OPE) promises to estimate the value of sequential triage policies from logged community-clinic data, but referral outcomes arrive late and selectively, so the logging policy and the target policy are confounded by the same unobserved severity that drives both the decision and the eventual label. the present analysis treats the validity of counterfactual triage estimators as a formal problem rather than an empirical one. It specifies a sequential decision model in which triage actions, delayed referral feedback and latent severity interact, and it derives the conditions under which importance-sampling, self-normalised and doubly robust estimators remain consistent when feedback is delayed and missing not at random. The central result is a bias decomposition that separates the delay-induced selection term from the variance term, and a proposition showing that doubly robust estimation removes the first-order selection bias only when the propensity model is correctly specified on the observed history. A replication-based evaluation of the ['Intercept', 'exposure', 'group', 'severity'] estimator was conducted: 600 data sets of N = 500 were drawn from a declared data-generating process (intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35, error SD 4.2), and the study characterises the behaviour of the ordinary least squares estimator under the stated process. Across the 600 replications the estimated bias was -0.00378 for the intercept and 0.00033 for exposure, with RMSE 0.8621 and 0.015 respectively, and empirical coverage of the nominal 95% intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The analysis clarifies which OPE estimators can be trusted for sequential triage and under what identification assumptions.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Referral for Retinopathy of Prematurity Under Variable Wide-Field Camera Availability: A Cascaded Calibration Evaluation of Healthcare Transfer Timing
items.abstract: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) remains a leading cause of preventable childhood blindness, and artificial intelligence (AI) referral systems based on wide-field digital retinal imaging have been proposed to extend screening into districts where ophthalmologists are scarce. Such systems are typically evaluated on image-level discrimination, yet their clinical value depends on a cascaded decision: an image must first be acquired with a camera that is available, then classified with a calibration that transfers across device makes, and only then converted into a transfer decision whose timing is safe. The analysis treats camera availability as a latent regime that governs both the probability of acquiring a gradable image and the calibration of the AI classifier, and it derives the distribution of referral timing error as a function of regime-conditional sensitivity, specificity and acquisition probability. Using a declared variance structure with an intraclass correlation of 0.64, a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0 and a residual standard deviation of 4.5, the design analysis shows that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5 percentage-point effect at 80% power. The framework clarifies why image-level performance metrics overstate referral safety when camera regimes are heterogeneous, and it identifies the calibration-transfer step as the dominant source of timing error under realistic availability constraints. The contribution is a design-level account of when cascaded AI referral can be trusted for ROP transfer decisions, and a specification of the evidence that a calibration-transfer evaluation must report.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Sparse-Identification of Antenatal Corticosteroid Timing Effects Under Variable Ultrasound Gestational-Age Dating Error: A Causal Discovery Evaluation of Healthcare Neonatal Respiratory Safety
items.abstract: Ultrasound gestational-age dating error is a persistent obstacle to estimating the effect of antenatal corticosteroid timing on neonatal respiratory outcomes, because misclassification of exposure and outcome can bias both conventional regression and machine-learning estimators. The framework combines a measurement-error model for gestational age with a sparsity-constrained score-based causal discovery algorithm, and it is assessed using a before-after-control-impact design with a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5, and an intraclass correlation of 0.64. Power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, and that the minimum detectable effect declines as cluster count increases. The framework is positioned as a methodological contribution to causal discovery in healthcare settings where gestational-age dating is imperfect, and its implications for neonatal respiratory safety evaluation are discussed.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Triage for Postpartum Hemorrhage Risk Under Variable Blood-Loss Estimation Practices: A Calibration-Transfer Evaluation of Transfusion-Trigger Thresholds
items.abstract: Postpartum hemorrhage remains a leading cause of maternal mortality, and artificial intelligence triage models that recommend transfusion are increasingly proposed to support clinical decisions in low-resource settings. These models are typically trained on visually estimated blood loss, yet visual estimation is known to be systematically biased and highly variable across clinicians and institutions. The problem is framed as a calibration-transfer problem: the mapping from true blood loss to recorded blood loss differs between practices, so a model learned under one mapping encounters a shifted input distribution at deployment. A formal framework is developed that separates the physiological signal from the estimation error, defines the calibration-transfer gap, and derives conditions under which a fixed threshold produces systematically different transfusion recommendations across practices. The analysis is theoretical and methodological; no observational data are used or claimed. The framework yields three results: a bias-variance decomposition of the transfer gap, a threshold-shift condition that quantifies how much a known estimation bias moves the effective trigger, and a sensitivity bound showing that the safety margin required for transfer grows with the variance of the estimation practice. The contribution is a precise characterisation of when calibration transfer fails and a set of design conditions under which an artificial intelligence triage model can be deployed across heterogeneous blood-loss estimation practices without silent erosion of its transfusion-trigger safety margin.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Tuberculosis Treatment Adherence Forecasting Under Variable Community Health Worker Smartphone Logging Gaps: A Missing-Not-At-Random Sensitivity Evaluation of Healthcare Loss-to-Follow-Up
items.abstract: Tuberculosis treatment adherence forecasting models trained on community health worker (CHW) smartphone logs face a structural problem: the logging process that generates the training signal is itself non-random, and the missingness mechanism is plausibly informative about the adherence outcome the model is meant to predict. The design parameters were fixed at between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, and intraclass correlation = 0.640; power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis is a design-characterisation study, not an empirical evaluation: no observational data are used or claimed. The framework distinguishes three logging-gap regimes (ignorable, covariate-dependent, and outcome-dependent) and derives the bias that each induces in the forecast target. The design analysis indicates that 56 clusters are required to detect a 5 percentage-point effect at 80% power under the declared variance structure, and that the minimum detectable effect at 80% power falls as cluster count rises from 8 to 32. The contribution is a sensitivity protocol that makes the MNAR assumption explicit and testable rather than silently absorbed into model training.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Ultrasound Interpretation for Placental Abruption Under Variable Portable Probe Acoustic Output Drift: A Test-Time Calibration Evaluation of Healthcare Referral Urgency
items.abstract: Portable ultrasound probes used in obstetric triage drift in acoustic output as transducers age and batteries discharge, and an artificial intelligence interpreter trained on stable cart-based images may therefore misclassify placental abruption at the point of care. the present analysis treats test-time calibration as a design problem for referral urgency rather than for image fidelity, and asks how much calibration is needed before an interpreter's urgency calls become safe under drift. A formal model of acoustic output drift is developed, a calibration operator is defined that rescales log-intensity features at inference, and the operating characteristics of the resulting referral rule are characterised under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD 6.0, residual SD 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64. Power was estimated across 2000 design cells for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effects of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points; 56 clusters were required for 5 percentage points at 80% power. Drift acts as a multiplicative bias on the decision statistic, that uncalibrated referral urgency is biased toward under-triage at low output and over-triage at high output, and that test-time calibration restores the decision threshold only when the drift estimate is itself unbiased. The contribution is a calibration-aware formulation of referral urgency that separates acoustic drift from pathological signal and specifies the cluster counts at which the separation can be evaluated.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Use and Training in Residency: Results of a National Family Medicine Survey
items.abstract: Purpose: We are in a time of rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in medical care and medical education. We sought to determine the patterns of use and training in AI among family medicine (FM) residents.Methods: The 2025 American Board of Family Medicine (ABFM) National Resident Survey (NRS) was administered in October 2025 to all FM residents who completed the In-Training Exam. Residents were asked about their use of AI in the last month and any education about AI use they received in the last 6 months. Resident demographics were obtained from ABFM administrative databases.Results: A total of 15,259 residents completed the AI questions (response rate: 99.6%) with 10,858 residents (71.1%) reporting they used AI in the last month. The most common uses reported were for medical reference (40.7%), clinical decision support (31.9%), learning outside of patient care (23.6%), and ambient documentation of clinical encounters (21.9%). Only 36% reported any AI education or training in the last 6 months.Conclusions: Most FM residents reported recent use of AI tools, reflecting integration of these technologies into routine educational and clinical activities. However, formal training on AI use appears limited, suggesting a gap between adoption and structured competency development. The widespread use of AI by family medicine trainees has risks and opportunities for our future primary care workforce that will require new critical appraisal skills and new methods for teaching and assessing clinical reasoning.

items.title: Assessing Workplace Technology Impacts on Employee Work and Wellbeing: A Post-Adoption Blind Spot
items.abstract: Organizations increasingly invest in adopting digital technologies to improve efficiency and competitiveness. Yet, in the post-adoption phase, these benefits depend on continued employee–technology interaction in everyday work, which can shape employee work and wellbeing and thereby influence organizational performance. Little is known, however, about how organizations assess these implications. Drawing on sociotechnical systems and performance measurement perspectives, this multiple-case study examines post-adoption assessment practices in eight Finnish organizations. The findings reveal a post-adoption blind spot: information on technology performance and use, employee work, and wellbeing was addressed through disconnected practices, indirect proxies, and informal judgements. Respondents reported recurring problems that remained weakly captured by current assessment: tool fragmentation, continuous adaptation demands, uneven performance effects, and work intensification, reflected more broadly in efficiency erosion and technology-related stress. The study conceptualizes integrated performance measurement systems as a potential mechanism for institutionalizing sociotechnical feedback through joint, recurring review of technology- and employee-related information.

items.title: Assessment Design Needs: A Preliminary Study on Using Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools for Educators
items.abstract: Assessment is considered as a key feature and central pillar in the teaching and learning process, particularly in making of judgement and measurement of student achievement and mastery of learning outcomes. The traditional methods of designing assessments items face several challenges, such as the need and requirement to design the assessment items manually, the time-consuming nature of the design process and the required cognitive skills through formal training provided by various institutions. As the result, the assessment items may lack on the detailed and context specific to validity and reliability, lack of standardized rubric and inconsistent scoring in performance based. A preliminary study was conducted at the analysis phase to explore fundamental understanding of Outcome-Based Education (OBE), Assessment Literacy, and Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) literacy among educators. Forty-six educators were involved in this study. Findings have shown that most of the respondents have lower level of using GAI tools and prompt engineering skills, 43.5% use GAI for teaching and learning, searching information (34.8%), idea collection process (6.5%), reflection/journal (4.3%), writing programming code (4.3%), generate image (4.3%) and other tasks (2.2%). The most difficult tasks are writing assessment test items (28.3%), practical tests (21.7%), presentations (17.4%), projects (10.9%), simulations (6.5%), and fieldwork (5.4%). The study shows that educators lack skills in designing assessment materials using GAI. Promoting a suitable guideline as a new innovative assessment tool will serve as a standardized guideline and as a means of incorporating AI ethically.

items.title: Associations between chicken farm environmental exposure and human surface microbiota and metabolite profiles: an exploratory pilot study
items.abstract: Chicken farms release various airborne pollutants that threaten farm workers’ occupational health, while the comprehensive impacts of chicken farm environmental exposures on human surface bacterial and metabolic homeostasis remain unclear. The niche-specific bacterial-metabolic interactions that are critical for host health regulation require systematic exploration. Three chicken farms with differential environmental conditions were selected, and 12 farm workers were recruited. Key atmospheric environmental parameters were monitored. 16S rRNA gene sequencing and non-targeted metabolomic analyses were performed to profile bacterial communities and metabolic characteristics of farm worker’ skin, oral, and nasal niches. Multiple bioinformatic and statistical analyses were adopted to explore niche-specific microecological variations and their correlations with environmental factors. Chicken farm environmental differences correlated with significant niche-specific microbial variations. Skin and nasal bacteria exhibited prominent farm-specific compositional divergence, whereas oral bacteria remained stable. Bacterial α diversity of nasal niche was markedly lower than that of skin and oral niches. Particulate matters, temperature and humidity were closely correlated with commensal bacterial taxa. Breeding exposures were statistically associated with altered metabolic pathways in skin and oral niches, while nasal metabolic characteristics remained relatively stable across different farms. Unique microbiota-metabolite interactions were identified, with skin bacteria specifically associated with tryptophan metabolism. This exploratory pilot study identified niche-specific correlational patterns between chicken farm environmental exposures and variations in human surface bacterial and metabolic profiles. The skin microecology exhibited the strongest correlational signal with farm-environment differences among the three surface niches. This study provided preliminary microbiota-metabolite observational evidence supporting occupational health risk assessment for chicken farm workers, while acknowledging inherent limitations of this cross-sectional pilot investigation.

items.title: Associations of patient safety-related perceptions and lifelong learning-related attitudes with critical trust in AI/digital clinical tools among medical students: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Patient safety, lifelong learning, and the safe use of artificial intelligence (AI) are increasingly relevant to undergraduate medical education, but their interrelationships remain poorly understood. This study examined medical students’ patient safety-related perceptions, lifelong learning-related attitudes, and critical trust in AI/digital clinical tools. This single-center cross-sectional survey was conducted at Gaziantep University Faculty of Medicine, Türkiye, between April and May 2026. Of 366 submitted responses, seven from students younger than 18 years were excluded, leaving 359 participants. Study-developed Likert-type item sets assessed patient safety, lifelong learning, and approaches to AI/digital clinical tools. Exploratory factor analysis, informed by parallel analysis, was used to derive exploratory indices. Associations were examined using nonparametric tests and multivariable linear regression, with sensitivity analyses using complete item sets and excluding invariant respondents. Patient safety training during the previous 12 months was reported by 72 students (20.1%), and AI/digital health or clinical decision support system training by 50 (13.9%). Among clinical-phase students, 10 of 79 (12.7%) reported having encountered an adverse-event or near-miss reporting system. The exploratory patient-safety index was positively correlated with the exploratory critical-trust index (Spearman’s ρ = 0.453, p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, the patient-safety index showed the largest standardized association with critical trust (B = 0.473, 95% CI 0.385 to 0.560; β = 0.507; p < 0.001). Clinical-phase status was positively associated with critical trust (B = 0.167, p = 0.010), whereas reported AI/digital health training was inversely associated (B = − 0.177, p = 0.018). The dichotomous any-use variable for digital clinical or AI-based tools was not independently associated with critical trust. In the complete-item sensitivity model, the patient-safety association persisted but was attenuated (β = 0.292, p < 0.001). Patient safety-related perceptions were associated with critical trust in AI/digital clinical tools, although the lower coefficient in the complete-item analysis indicates that the estimated magnitude was sensitive to how the scores were constructed; differences in item composition, measurement reliability, and wording-related structure may also have contributed. These exploratory cross-sectional findings do not establish causal or curricular effects but provide a rationale for longitudinal, interventional, and simulation-based studies examining how patient safety, lifelong learning, and critical evaluation of AI-supported recommendations may intersect in medical education.
